_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for intelligent-design, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Separate what is measured from what is meant
items.summary: Both matter. Do not confuse them.

items.title: Spend an evening watching one natural system, a tide pool or an anthill
items.summary: Describe the design you see, then ask how it came to be.

items.title: Look for the original study behind a news story
items.summary: The paper is almost always more careful than the headline.

items.title: Note what a result does not show
items.summary: Limits are part of the finding.

items.title: Learn the difference between correlation and cause
items.summary: It is the most useful idea in everyday statistics.

items.title: Keep a nature journal for a month
items.summary: One observation a day. By the end you will see a season change.

items.title: Visit a lab or observatory open day
items.summary: Scientists are often delighted to be asked questions.

items.title: Read one paper a week from outside your field
items.summary: Even partial understanding opens new connections.

items.title: iNaturalist
items.summary: Identify plants and animals and share observations with scientists.

items.title: Stellarium
items.summary: A free planetarium that shows the sky from where you are.

items.title: arXiv
items.summary: Free preprints of research papers.

items.title: Join a citizen-science project
items.summary: Count birds, classify galaxies or log rainfall for real researchers.

items.title: Volunteer at a science museum
items.summary: Explaining an idea is the best way to learn it.

items.title: Write the opposite of your opinion as fairly as you can
items.summary: If you cannot state the other side so its holders agree, you do not understand it yet.

items.title: Read one primary text instead of three summaries
items.summary: Original voices surprise you in ways summaries cannot.

items.title: Start a one-chapter reading group
items.summary: Small enough to finish, deep enough to argue about.

items.title: Hold a debate where each side argues the position they reject
items.summary: It is the fastest way to find the weak spots in your own view.

items.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
items.summary: Free, peer-reviewed articles on philosophical topics.

items.title: Project Gutenberg
items.summary: Free ebooks of classic works whose copyright has expired.

items.title: Audit a free philosophy or history course
items.summary: Many universities publish full courses at no cost.
